To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the modal analysis of a structure can be used to identify its structural relevance, (2) this is particularly true for old structures, (3) the structural relevance of a structure is not only related to its structural typology, (4) it can be related to its construction history.

“The calibration of a FE model of a structure by means of ambient noise modal analysis is an important step in the seismic FE analysis, but it is not enough to ensure the reliability of the analysis”.

1) the numerical model of the Perret tower has to be calibrated with the modal frequencies measured by the ambient noise modal analysis and 2) the modal analysis has to be performed by considering the whole structure, including the foundations and the basement, and by considering only the structural components of the tower.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the most significant components of the structure, which have to be modeled with a high level of detail, in order to obtain a reliable numerical model.
the identification of the structural parameters that can be considered as “calibration” parameters, i.e. the parameters that can be used to calibrate the numerical model.
the following issues: - how to perform a reliable FE model of a complex structure, - how to validate the numerical model, - how to perform the non-linear analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the calibration is an indispensable step in the process of the seismic analysis of a structure.
the calibration of the FE model by means of in situ measurements is a very useful and necessary step in the seismic analysis of an old RC building.

the calibration of the numerical model is a necessary step in the seismic assessment of a structure, but it is not sufficient to guarantee that the results of the non-linear dynamic analysis are reliable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the calibration is an essential phase for a correct and reliable numerical analysis of a structure.
a careful calibration of the FE model of the Perret tower has been carried out by using the modal analysis performed by means of Ambient Noise.

the Perret Tower is a very interesting case study for the seismic analysis of an old RC structure because the building is very complex in terms of structural behavior, the FE model is very complex in the details of modeling and the in-situ measurements are difficult to perform and to be interpreted.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the modal analysis is a powerful tool for the validation of the numerical model of the building, but it has to be performed on a set of sensors placed in strategic positions.

the modal analysis of the Perrett tower has shown the presence of some structural anomalies, such as the presence of some cracks in the concrete and the lack of the connection between the beams and the columns, that could be the cause of the damage observed after the seismic event.

a correct calibration of the numerical model of the building requires a careful analysis of the modal measurements in order to identify the relevant modes of the structure and the corresponding FE models.
